Capture runs on every completed turn and does not interrupt the session.</p></div><div aria-hidden="true" class="invisible col-start-1 row-start-1"><h3 class="font-display text-primary text-lg font-medium leading-tight tracking-tight">Stored as markdown</h3><p class="text-primary/60 [&amp;_code]:text-primary/80 mt-2 text-sm leading-relaxed text-pretty [&amp;_code]:font-mono [&amp;_code]:text-[0.9em]">Notes are markdown files, one topic per subject. Each project has its own workspace scope, and a global scope holds preferences that apply everywhere. <code>/dream</code> merges new observations into the topic they belong to, and <code>/memory</code> shows the files as they are on disk.</p></div><div aria-hidden="true" class="invisible col-start-1 row-start-1"><h3 class="font-display text-primary text-lg font-medium leading-tight tracking-tight">Read back in later sessions</h3><p class="text-primary/60 [&amp;_code]:text-primary/80 mt-2 text-sm leading-relaxed text-pretty [&amp;_code]:font-mono [&amp;_code]:text-[0.9em]">Before starting related work, Grok reads the topics that cover the area and applies them, including in sessions where the subject never comes up. Instructions in the current conversation take precedence over anything in a note.</p></div><div class="relative col-start-1 row-start-1"><div class="absolute inset-x-0 top-0" style="opacity:1"><h3 class="font-display text-primary text-lg font-medium leading-tight tracking-tight">Captured after the turn</h3><p class="text-primary/60 [&amp;_code]:text-primary/80 mt-2 text-sm leading-relaxed text-pretty [&amp;_code]:font-mono [&amp;_code]:text-[0.9em]">After a turn completes, Grok reviews it in the background and records anything durable: conventions, decisions, and project facts. Capture runs on every completed turn and does not interrupt the session.</p></div></div></div></div><h2 id="what-it-remembers"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#what-it-remembers">What it remembers</a></h2><p>Memory holds the details most likely to matter in a later session: how the team writes and reviews code, decisions and the reasoning behind them, and durable facts about the project, from where a subsystem lives to which command runs the suite. Task state, tentative conclusions, secrets, and anything the repository or its docs already cover are left out.</p><p>Notes are kept per project, plus a global set for preferences that apply everywhere.</p><h2 id="written-in-the-background"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#written-in-the-background">Written in the background</a></h2><p>Capture runs after a turn completes and never blocks the session. Grok reviews the finished turn, writes anything worth keeping as a markdown note, and continues. Over time, <code>/dream</code> folds those notes into topic files, one per subject, so each project ends up with a small set of organized references.</p><p>When you return to a project, Grok reads the topics that cover the area it is about to work in. Instructions in the current conversation take precedence over anything in a note.</p><h2 id="browsing-memory"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#browsing-memory">Browsing memory</a></h2><p><code>/memory</code> opens a read-only browser of every memory file, grouped by scope, with a preview of the selected file. It is the fastest way to see what a session produced, and to find the file to edit when a note is wrong.</p><div class="relative not-prose my-12"><div class="relative p-8 sm:p-10 lg:p-12 <li><code>/dream</code> organizes recent notes into topic files, for example <code>topics/testing.md</code>. Dream also runs on its own periodically in the background.</li>
</ul><h2 id="availability"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#availability">Availability</a></h2><p>Memory is available in Grok Build now.
